title: Remapping right shift also affects left shift.
author: Rashastt

status.label: Implementation-grade Shift-side fix design ready
status.detail: The current low-level keyboard hook forwards the raw vkCode into the editor capture flow, while the save/apply path expands a generic Shift mapping to both physical Shift keys. That makes a right-Shift-only remap designable now.

next_action.label: Approve the physical Shift-side capture fix
next_action.reason: The failing mechanism, affected files, and focused regression tests are identified without needing more reporter evidence.

judgment.rationale: The report is short but decisive, and the current code path clearly explains it: KeyboardHook.cpp forwards the raw low-level hook vkCode without decoding the physical Shift side, the editor capture path records that value as the original key, and LoadingAndSavingRemappingHelper expands a generic Shift mapping to both left and right Shift during save/apply.
evidence: The issue says remapping right Shift causes left Shift to perform the same remap even though only right Shift was configured.
Current keyboard_layout.cpp distinguishes Shift (Left) and Shift (Right), so the UI and storage model already have side-specific names available.
Current KeyboardHook.cpp forwards reinterpret_cast<KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT*>(lParam)->vkCode directly into the managed KeyboardEvent without decoding the physical Shift side from scanCode.
Current LoadingAndSavingRemappingHelper.cpp expands a generic VK_SHIFT original key into both VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT when building the remap table.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a narrow fix that decodes the physical Shift side before Keyboard Manager records remaps and add regression tests that prove a right-Shift remap stays right-Shift only.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers this side-specific Keyboard Manager capture bug, and the current code path identifies a precise root cause and narrow implementation boundary.

proposed_fixes.title: Decode physical Shift side before Keyboard Manager records remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The shared low-level keyboard hook currently publishes the raw vkCode to the managed editor capture path. For Shift, that can remain generic instead of side-specific, so the editor stores VK_SHIFT as the original key and the remap loader expands that generic mapping to both VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT.
plan: Decode generic low-level hook modifier keys to their physical side before they become KeyboardEvent.ev.key, using scanCode and flags from KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT.
Keep the captured side-specific key all the way through Keyboard Manager editor formatting and key-code round-tripping so Right Shift remains VK_RSHIFT instead of collapsing to VK_SHIFT.
Add focused regressions proving that right-Shift-only capture saves a right-Shift-only mapping and that a generic Shift mapping still deliberately expands to both sides when chosen intentionally.
verification: Capture and save a Right Shift remap, then confirm only Right Shift triggers the remap while Left Shift remains unchanged.
Capture and save a Left Shift remap and confirm the inverse behavior.
Intentionally choose generic Shift and confirm the save/apply path still expands to both physical sides.

confidence.rationale: The current capture and save/apply code paths line up directly with the user-visible symptom, and the fix boundary is narrow and testable.

issue_context.summary: A right-Shift-only remap is being captured or saved as generic Shift, so the save/apply path turns it into a both-sides remap. The current hook and remap-loading code make the failing mechanism explicit enough for an implementation-grade design.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
The affected area is Keyboard Manager.
The issue states that remapping Right Shift also affects Left Shift.
There are no comments, attachments, assignees, or linked work on the live issue.
Current keyboard_layout.cpp exposes distinct names for Shift (Left) and Shift (Right).
inferences: The product intends to support side-specific modifier keys because it already names and stores them distinctly.
The bug is likely in key-capture normalization rather than in the later runtime remap lookup, because the save/apply path already has special handling for a generic Shift source key.
issue_context.analysis: The issue needs no more reporter evidence. The current low-level hook and remap-loader code expose a clear cause-and-effect chain that explains why a right-Shift remap can become a both-sides remap. That makes this the single full-design candidate in the batch.

actions.label: Approve physical Shift-side capture fix

design.title: Decode physical Shift side before Keyboard Manager records remaps

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream code, PR, comment, or issue write is authorized by this artifact.

design.root_cause: Keyboard Manager records a side-specific Shift remap through a shared low-level keyboard hook that currently emits the raw vkCode without decoding the physical Shift side. When the recorded source key collapses to generic VK_SHIFT, the existing save/apply logic intentionally expands that generic source to both VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT, so a right-Shift-only remap becomes a both-sides remap.
evidence: Observed: KeyboardHook.cpp assigns KeyboardEvent.ev.key from KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT.vkCode directly.
Observed: keyboard_layout.cpp has separate key names for Shift (Left) and Shift (Right), proving the UI/storage model expects side-specific Shift keys.
Observed: LoadingAndSavingRemappingHelper.cpp expands a generic VK_SHIFT source into both VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT when building the single-key remap table.
Inferred: once the editor capture path stores VK_SHIFT instead of VK_RSHIFT, the later both-sides expansion exactly matches the user-visible symptom.

affected_files.purpose: Publishes low-level keyboard events to managed hotkey consumers and currently forwards raw vkCode without physical-side decoding.
Managed bridge used by Keyboard Manager and other shortcut controls to receive KeyboardEvent.ev.key.
Captures the incoming key identity, formats it for the editor, and preserves the recorded original key order.
Expands generic modifier source keys to both physical sides during save/apply.
Maps virtual-key codes to display names and already exposes side-specific Shift labels.
Existing interop test project that can host a deterministic regression seam for low-level key decoding.
Existing Keyboard Manager editor save/apply test suite that can verify generic Shift still expands only when intentionally chosen.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The shared low-level keyboard hook constructs KeyboardEvent by copying only KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT.vkCode into ev.key. For Shift, that loses the physical side before any managed consumer sees the event.
implementation_steps.change: Introduce a small helper that decodes the physical virtual key from KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT using scanCode and flags, and use the decoded key when populating KeyboardEvent.ev.key. Preserve the raw vkCode for non-ambiguous keys and fall back safely if decoding fails.
edge_cases: Do not break Ctrl/Alt/Win or ordinary action keys that already arrive with an unambiguous virtual key.
Keep the hook callback allocation-free and free of I/O so it remains safe in the low-level hook path.
If scan-code decoding ever fails, fall back to the existing vkCode instead of dropping the event.
tests: Add an interop regression seam that proves a synthetic VK_SHIFT event with left and right scan codes resolves to VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT.
Keep existing shortcut-control and keyboard-manager capture behavior unchanged for non-Shift keys.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Keyboard Manager trusts the key identity supplied by the shared hook and immediately formats it for display and later key-code round-tripping.
implementation_steps.change: Verify the editor capture path preserves the now-side-specific key all the way through formatting and saving. No new generic coalescing should convert Right Shift back to Shift during capture or display-name round-tripping.
edge_cases: Retain canonical modifier ordering in the display string even when the captured modifier is side-specific.
Continue allowing an intentionally generic Shift choice from dropdown-based selection flows.
tests: Manual or automated capture of Right Shift should show Shift (Right) in the editor and persist the right-side key code.
Left Shift capture should remain side-specific and not conflict with a stored right-side mapping.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The save/apply path intentionally expands a generic VK_SHIFT source into both VK_LSHIFT and VK_RSHIFT. That is correct only when the user really chose generic Shift.
implementation_steps.change: Leave generic-both-sides expansion intact, but add regression coverage proving that side-specific keys bypass the generic expansion and remain one-sided when the capture flow records VK_RSHIFT or VK_LSHIFT.
edge_cases: Do not regress the intentionally generic modifier behavior for users who truly want both Shift keys remapped.
Preserve the existing combine-both-sides optimization only when both explicit sides map to the same target.
tests: Extend LoadingAndSavingRemappingTests.cpp with a right-Shift-only source mapping and assert that the resulting table contains only VK_RSHIFT for that remap.
Retain the existing tests that generic VK_SHIFT expands to both sides and that paired explicit modifiers can still combine when they intentionally share the same target.

verify: Build the shared interop component with: pwsh .\tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\src\common\interop\PowerToys.Interop.vcxproj

Build the Keyboard Manager editor tests with: pwsh .\tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\src\modules\KeyboardManager\KeyboardManagerEditorTest\KeyboardManagerEditorTest.vcxproj
Run the interop tests with: dotnet test .\src\common\interop\interop-tests\Common.Interop.UnitTests.csproj -c Debug

Run the Keyboard Manager editor tests from the built test binary or Visual Studio Test Explorer, focusing on the new right-Shift roundtrip regression and the existing generic-modifier expansion tests.
Manually capture a Right Shift remap in the new Keyboard Manager editor, save it, then verify only Right Shift triggers the remap while Left Shift behaves normally.
risks: The shared hook is used outside Keyboard Manager, so decoding must remain additive and not change non-ambiguous keys.
Ctrl and Alt have their own left/right semantics and should be audited so a future generic-vkCode ambiguity does not get worse while fixing Shift.
Any new test seam in the interop layer must stay deterministic and avoid requiring an actual global keyboard hook in CI.
alternatives: Collapse both Shift keys intentionally in the editor: rejected because the product already exposes side-specific Shift names and the reporter specifically expects right-side-only behavior.
Patch only the save/apply path to special-case Right Shift guesses: rejected because the root cause is earlier capture-time loss of physical-side identity.
Fix only the runtime engine lookup: rejected because the bug begins when the editor records a generic Shift source key, and the same shared hook is also used by other shortcut capture controls.
